fixes.explanation: Close, friend, but the verse goes the other way. It says "…if you truly call out to insight and lift your voice to understanding…" (Proverbs 2:3). The son isn't sitting quietly. He's calling out and lifting his voice. That's LOUD, not a silent wait.

Yes, friend. The writer says "…if you seek it like silver and search it out like hidden treasure…" (Proverbs 2:4). Silver and hidden treasure are things people search hard for. That's the kind of seeking the son is told to do.

That's it, friend. "For the LORD gives wisdom; from His mouth come knowledge and understanding." (Proverbs 2:6). The son does the searching, and the LORD does the giving. Knowledge and understanding come from His mouth.

True, friend. Verse 8 says He acts "…to guard the paths of justice and protect the way of His saints." (Proverbs 2:8). So the LORD guards the paths of justice, and He protects the way of His saints. That's a good thing to have on your side.

I see why that might sound right, friend, because knowledge can sound heavy. But the verse says "…wisdom will enter your heart, and knowledge will delight your soul." (Proverbs 2:10). Delight is the opposite of a heavy load. So this one is false.

That's right. The verse says "…wisdom will enter your heart, and knowledge will delight your soul." (Proverbs 2:10). Knowledge doesn't weigh the soul down. It delights it. I'd take that kind of delight any day, friend.
True, friend. Verse 14 describes them as "…those who enjoy doing evil and rejoice in the twistedness of evil…" (Proverbs 2:14). They enjoy it and rejoice in it. I think this one is heavy.

That's right, friend. Verse 19 says "None who go to her return or negotiate the paths of life." (Proverbs 2:19). The verse says none who go to her return, and none negotiate the paths of life. It's a heavy warning, and that's why wisdom guards the son from it.

Yes, friend. Verse 20 says "So you will follow in the ways of the good, and keep to the paths of the righteous." (Proverbs 2:20). With wisdom guarding him, the son follows in the ways of the good. That's the road wisdom leads him down.

Yes, friend. Verse 21 says "…the upright will inhabit the land, and the blameless will remain in it…" (Proverbs 2:21). The upright inhabit the land, and the blameless remain in it. I'd say that's a good promise to hear.

Leaving is the opposite of what the verse says. It says "…the upright will inhabit the land, and the blameless will remain in it…" (Proverbs 2:21). The upright inhabit the land, and the blameless remain in it, friend.
